2. VOCABULARY SPIRAL (W75-W77 Geography): Fill in the blank: The ___ plates move slowly under the ocean / The volcano created new ___ / Scientists use ___ systems to warn people. (Word bank: tectonic, land, warning)
3. MATH SPIRAL: A town was flooded for 6 days. The water level on Day 1 was 1m. If it rose 0.5m each day, what was the level on Day 6? How many times higher than Day 1?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Natural disasters are extreme events caused by natural forces. They can cause great damage to people, buildings, and the environment. The most common types include earthquakes, floods, and volcanic eruptions.
content: 📖 Natural disasters are extreme events caused by natural forces. They can cause great damage to people, buildings, and the environment. The most common types include earthquakes, floods, and volcanic eruptions.

An earthquake happens when tectonic plates — huge pieces of Earth's outer shell — suddenly move against each other. This releases energy in waves, causing the ground to shake. Earthquakes near cities can destroy buildings and roads.

Floods occur when too much water overflows onto normally dry land. Heavy rainfall, melting snow, or storms can cause rivers to burst their banks. Floods destroy crops, damage homes, and contaminate water supplies.

Volcanic eruptions happen when molten rock called magma pushes up through cracks in Earth's surface. Lava, ash, and gases pour out of the volcano. Although eruptions can be dangerous, they also create new land and make soil very fertile for farming.
Governments use early warning systems to alert people before disasters strike, giving communities time to evacuate and prepare.

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — STEM/CLIL Connection
content: -> MATH VOCABULARY: scale, ratio, measure, Richter scale, magnitude, compare, proportional
-> CONCEPT: The Richter scale measures earthquake strength. Each step up means the earthquake is 10× stronger!
->   Magnitude 4 = minor | Magnitude 5 = moderate | Magnitude 6 = strong | Magnitude 7 = major | Magnitude 8+ = great
->   • A magnitude 6 earthquake is 10 times stronger than a magnitude 5 earthquake.
->   • The ratio of Mag 7 to Mag 5 strength is 100:1 (because 10×10 = 100).
-> GUIDED WORD PROBLEM: Japan had a magnitude 5 earthquake in 2019 and a magnitude 7 earthquake in 2011.
->   Q1: How many times stronger was the 2011 earthquake? (Ans: 10×10 = 100 times)
